question: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is a scalar quantity, which means it only has magnitude and no direction.
 
• On the other hand, **force**, **acceleration**, and **velocity** are vector quantities that have both magnitude and direction.
 
• Understanding the distinction between scalar and vector quantities is fundamental in physics as it affects how they are added, subtracted, and applied in various equations.
 
• Scalar quantities are described by a single number and units, while vector quantities require both magnitude and direction for a complete description.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In physics, **vectors** are often represented graphically by arrows, where the length of the arrow indicates the magnitude and the direction of the arrow indicates the direction of the vector.
 
• **Scalars** can be added, subtracted, multiplied, and divided like ordinary numbers, while vector operations follow specific rules, such as vector addition and vector multiplication.
 
• Common examples of scalar quantities include temperature, distance, and time, whereas common vector quantities include velocity, displacement, and electric field strength.
 
• Understanding the nature of quantities as scalar or vector is crucial in solving problems related to motion, forces, and other physical phenomena.
